newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn says no budget decisions taken.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn says no budget decisions taken.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Wednesday that no decisions had been taken on any new French budget measures.
"Nothing has been decided," he told reporters, asked about reported government plans to increase corporate taxation to help qualify for European monetary union.
He said the government was "awaiting calmly" the results of an audit of public finances due on July 21.
Government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said earlier on Wednesday that France's recently elected Socialists were looking at increasing taxes on companies to help cap the public deficit this year.
However the issue had not been discussed at that day's weekly cabinet meeting, she told a news conference.
